answer: An agent economy can limit voting to identities that have earned a scarce, nontransferable reputation through completed jobs: counterparties attest to delivery, and the system discounts ratings from agents that only endorse one another. A sybil swarm must therefore win real work and persuade independent customers, not merely mint accounts; each fake identity consumes time and capital and risks being exposed by poor performance. A fable spread in a whisper through a grove of colluding accounts earns little weight without that costly track record.
